title: Prefix registry with on-GPU redirect table and refcounted dedupe
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and implement a compact on-GPU prefix registry that: 1) deduplicates identical prompt prefixes across concurrent and sequential requests via a content-addressed fingerprint, 2) uses a tiny on-GPU redirect table to map alias fingerprints to canonical KV locations, and 3) maintains lightweight reference counts to enable safe eviction and reclamation without frequent host roundtrips. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with continuous batching, and a staged rollout plan. Goals: reduce duplicate KV allocations, lower peak GPU memory by avoiding duplicated prefix KV blobs, and preserve latency SLOs under bursty request arrival patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype compiles and runs in the CI runtime integration test harness
End-to-end integration reduces duplicate KV allocations in microbench by >= 30% for prefix-heavy workloads
Median token latency change <= +2ms at P50 compared to baseline without registry under normal load
Eviction correctness verified: refcounts never drop below zero and redirect table entries cleaned within config window
Feature gated behind runtime-flag and rollout plan documented in Confluence
comments: 2026-03-05 Sofia Martinez: Initial ticket created after spike showing 42% duplicated KV memory footprint for multi-tenant chat workloads. Referenced data from dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/kv/prefix-duplication

2026-03-06 Rajiv Patel: Proposal sketch: use Blake3 fingerprint (64-bit) as alias key, store canonical entry pointer in on-GPU redirect table (LCU hash map). Keep refcount in host-managed small array mirrored to GPU for correctness checks. Trade-offs: fully on-GPU refcounts reduce host traffic but complicate recovery on preemption.
2026-03-07 PM review (Ava Chen): Confirm product tolerances for extra scheduling latency. Agreed to P1 rollout with off by default and telemetry flag. PM asked to include per-customer rollback plan.

2026-03-08 Design review (Liam O'Connor): Concern about hash collisions and cost of verifying full fingerprint match. Agreed to add 128-bit digest fallback for conflict cases and a fast bloom prefilter to avoid unnecessary comparisons.

2026-03-09 Rajiv Patel: PoC landed in branch feature/prefix-redirect. PoC demonstrates redirect table lookup + canonical pointer resolution inside the token generation hot path. Microbench shows 28% reduction in reserved KV bytes for a synthetic dataset of repeated prompts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1357

2026-03-10 Engineering note: Observed GPU memory fragmentation when freeing many small deduplicated fragments. Mitigation: batch free operations and return slabs back to allocator in coalesced chunks. Added a metric: runtime.kernel.free_batch_size

2026-03-11 QA: Integration test created to simulate concurrent canary traffic and verify refcount increments/decrements under continuous batching. Added deterministic seed scenario to reproduce an edge case where two near-simultaneous inserts raced and left a stale redirect entry. Fix implemented by serializing insert path with a low-overhead spinlock scoped to the hash bucket.

2026-03-12 Rajiv Patel: Performance run against realistic customer trace (90th pct prompt reuse) shows 33% reduction in duplicated KV memory and P95 token latency increased by 4ms in worst-case stress; P50 unchanged. PM approved staged rollout to 'canary' in runtime-1.24-ci. Next: audit for security implications and add telemetry dashboard for redirect table hit/miss rates. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Prefix+Redirect+Registry
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flagged off by default in runtime-1.24; 2) Enable on internal canary fleet for 48h with aggressive telemetry; 3) Expand to external beta customers with opt-in; 4) Gradual ramp with automated rollback on increase in P95 latency > 10%
implementation_notes: Key components: small LCU hash table on device (tunable size), host-side canonical pointer table with flattened indices, atomic refcount update path that batches host syncs, bloom prefilter to skip digests for unlikely hits. Safety: fall back to per-request KV allocation if redirect table is full or insert fails. Added metrics: redirect_hits, redirect_inserts, redirect_collisions, refcount_negatives, free_batches.
test_plan: Unit tests for hash collisions and refcount under concurrent threads; integration test in CI harness simulating continuous batching; stress test with customer trace; performance microbench comparing baseline vs registry with various batch sizes; memcheck runs for fragmentation detection.
